subject.name_or_desc: King Charles I and Queen Henrietta Maria (the quesiteds); the querent unnamed

context.question: (1) If his Majesty should procure forces out of Ireland to harm the Parliament? (2) If the Queen, then in the North, would advance with her army, prosper, and when his Majesty should meet her?
context.asked_at: Not stated in the chapter; the figure precedes the crossing of 11 April 1643 referred to in the judgment.
context.setting: One figure answering two war questions: whether the King would procure Irish forces against the Parliament, and whether the Queen, then in the North with an army, would advance, prosper, and meet the King.

attachments.key_positions: His Majesty signified by the Moon in Cancer in the tenth house, in her own house, increasing in light, and void of all infelicity except slowness in motion; the Sun, lord of the eleventh (the house signifying assistance or aid), posited in the seventh in his exaltation, applying to the cusp of the eleventh but wanting six degrees of being partill, and in direct opposition to the Ascendant (the Parliament); the Queen's significatrix Saturn, lord of the fourth (being the seventh from the tenth), removing out of one sign into another and going into Aries, his fall; the Moon wanting three or four degrees of the trine of Saturn
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.chapter: Book II, the chapter following Chap. LXXXV: if his Majesty should procure forces out of Ireland; if the Queen would advance with her army, and when his Majesty should meet her
